name: nine_thousand_torches
revision: r3 (2026-11-10): motive tightened: L06 ties the nightly door torch to L03's spawn rule ('so nothing SPAWNS'), L14 names it ('Every night at ONCE'); the wave stays in the picture (S14) unsaid
caption: who put 6,000 torches on my village 🔥
logline: A villager kid wakes to find a torch on every block of his village and thinks something terrible is coming, but follows the last growing row to his own door, where his best friend, the village's player, places the final torch, the one he used to place there every night, and leaves the game for good.
question: why tf is there a torch on every single block of this village?
premise: One morning a plains village wakes up with a torch on every grass block, fence post, roof ridge and hay bale: six thousand of them. The villager kid who tells it knows zombies can't spawn on a lit block, so he decides something big must be coming. Jonah, the player who lives in the village and his best friend, puts a torch by the kid's door every night, then says 'see you tomorrow' and logs off. Yesterday Jonah said his mom made him promise, one last night, which the kid reads as Jonah being grounded again. This morning all of Jonah's things are in the kid's family chest and Jonah's house is gone, just a square of torches. One row is still growing round a corner; the kid wants to know who, and follows it to his own door.
twist: Nothing is coming: Jonah is going. Every night he lit the kid's door before he logged off; he is leaving the world for good (his mom's rule: one last night), so he did every night at once: a torch on every block of the village, so no zombie can ever spawn in it with nobody left to light it. He took his own house down so it wouldn't be one dark room left behind, gave everything he owned to his best friend, and saved the door spot for the last torch, the same spot as every night. He places it, waves, and leaves the game. This time the chat shows no 'see you tomorrow', because it isn't true. The torches are the goodbye.
